questions.question: In React 19, which hook is best suited for wrapping expensive state updates so that user typing and clicking interactions remain non-blocking at 60fps?
options: useEffect
useMemo
useTransition
useLayoutEffect
questions.explanation: useTransition allows marking state updates as non-blocking transitions, prioritizing critical user gestures while deferring heavyweight tree updates.

questions.question: When designing a reducer function in modern React or Redux, which of the following is a mandatory contract?
options: It must make asynchronous fetch calls directly
It must be a pure function with no side effects and deterministic return value
It must mutate the incoming state directly to save allocations
It must store state in window.localStorage automatically
questions.explanation: Reducers must always be pure functions: given the same state and action payload, they must return the exact same output with zero side effects.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of Context multiplexing (splitting State Context from Dispatch Context)?
options: It increases the bundle size for better compression
Components that only trigger dispatch actions will not re-render when state values update
It automatically saves state to cookies
It converts React components into web components
questions.explanation: By separating State Context from Dispatch Context, child components that only dispatch actions never re-render when state changes.

questions.question: Why should array indices generally be avoided as keys in dynamic React lists?
options: React throws a compile error if an index is used
Indices cause reconciliation bugs and state leakage when items are reordered, inserted, or removed
Index keys disable CSS styles
Index keys make the page reload on click
questions.explanation: Reusing array indices across list mutations breaks React Fiber's identity tracking, causing DOM nodes and local state to bind to the wrong items.

questions.question: In a production Docker container deployment for a Next.js application, why are multi-stage builds recommended?
options: They enable multiple operating systems in one container
They exclude development dependencies and compiler artifacts, minimizing image size and attack surface
They automatically register the domain with DNS
They run unit tests faster in the browser
questions.explanation: Multi-stage Docker builds discard build tools, devDependencies, and raw source files, shipping only the optimized runtime bundle in a secure, compact image.
